before.html:
Question 1
?

The displacement (in centimeters) of an ant moving in a straight line is given by s(t)=t2+3t, where t is measured in seconds. Find the ant's acceleration at t=10 seconds.

a
10 cm/s2
b
15 cm/s2
c
4 cm/s2
d
2 cm/s2
e
8 cm/s2
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of displacement: s'(t)=2t+3 and s''(t)=2. Thus at t=10 seconds, the acceleration is 2 cm/s².

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The displacement (in centimeters) of an ant moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)={t}^{2}+3t,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds.
Find the ant's acceleration at $t=10$ seconds.
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+3t) \\  & =2t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+3) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=10,$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
a(10)=2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration when $t=10$ seconds is $2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

verification.explanation: Differentiating twice gives v(t)=2t+3 and a(t)=2, so a(10)=2 cm/s². The worked solution confirms the value 2 but mistakenly labels the units m/s²; displacement is given in centimeters. Option d is correct.

Question 2
?

The velocity v of a particle at time t is given by v(t)=3ln⁡t+t3−2t2. Calculate the acceleration of the particle at time t.

a
a(t)=−3t+3t2−4t
b
a(t)=3t+3t2−4t2
c
a(t)=3t+3t2−4t
d
a(t)=−3t−3t2−4t
e
a(t)=t3+3t2−4t
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity. Differentiating each term gives a(t)=3/t+3t²−4t, which matches option c.
